solution:
Interpret the matrix as the adjacency matrix of a simple bipartite graph with 5 labeled vertices on each side. Every vertex has degree 2, so the graph is a disjoint union of alternating cycles. A component using k vertices from each side, for k≥2, can be chosen in \(\binom{5}{k}^2\) ways and arranged as an alternating cycle in \(k!(k-1)!/2\) ways. The possible component-size partitions of 5 are 5, 3+2, and 2+2+1 (the last is impossible since a degree-2 simple bipartite graph has no component of size 1). Thus only 5 and 3+2 occur.

For one 5-cycle, the count is \(5!4!/2=1440\). For components of sizes 3 and 2, choose the size-3 vertices on each side and form both cycles:
\[\binom53^2\frac{3!2!}{2}\frac{2!1!}{2}=100\cdot6\cdot1=600.\]
Total: \(1440+600=2040\).
insight: A simple bipartite graph in which every vertex has degree 2 is a disjoint union of even cycles.
insight_justification: Starting at any vertex and following successive edges must eventually close a cycle; degree 2 leaves no branch or endpoint, and each connected component is therefore a cycle. Bipartiteness makes each such cycle alternate between the two vertex parts.
